title: IDGEN-138: RemoteIdentifierSourceProcessor supports fetching identifiers through the REST API
body:
https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/IDGEN-138

`RemoteIdentifierSourceProcessor` sends a form post to `exportIdentifiers.form`, which fails against current platforms for two reasons:
- **CSRF protection:** CSRFGuard rejects the post, because only `/ws/*` is excluded by default.
- **Authentication module:** with a web authentication scheme such as 2FA, the controller's `Context.authenticate(username, password)` fails with `authentication.error.incorrectCredentialsForScheme`.

### Fetching identifiers through the REST API
When a `RemoteIdentifierSource` url is under `/ws/rest/`, the processor calls the existing REST endpoint (`POST /ws/rest/v1/idgen/identifiersource` with `generateIdentifiers`), which avoids both problems:
- It posts a JSON body (`generateIdentifiers`, `sourceUuid`, `numberToGenerate`, `comment`), taking `sourceUuid` and `comment` from the url's query parameters, eg. `https://server/openmrs/ws/rest/v1/idgen/identifiersource?sourceUuid=<uuid>&comment=<comment>`.
- It sends the source's user and password as a Basic `Authorization` header.
- It accepts any 2xx response, since REST responds with 201.
- It uses HttpClient's current defaults, eg. strict hostname verification.
- The url must be to the `identifiersource` resource itself. A url to a specific source (eg. `.../identifiersource/<uuid>`) is rejected, because a post there would update that source on the remote server rather than generate identifiers.

Other urls keep the existing form post to `exportIdentifiers.form`. That request is unchanged: same client and hostname verification, and it still requires 200. The only additions are connect (30s) and socket (5 minutes) timeouts, and closing the client after each request, so an unresponsive remote server can't hang the pool refill. REST requests use the same timeouts.

### Serving servers that still use exportIdentifiers.form
The `exportIdentifiers.form` controller no longer authenticates again when the request is already authenticated as the user named by the `username` parameter. With a web authentication scheme, the authentication filter has already logged that user in, and authenticating again always fails. Any other request authenticates as before. This lets servers that haven't upgraded keep getting identifiers from an upgraded server, as long as that server also excludes the url from CSRF protection, eg. with the runtime property `org.owasp.csrfguard.unprotected.idgenexport=%servletContext%/module/idgen/exportIdentifiers.form`.

### Testing
- Unit tests make full requests to a local HTTP server for each kind of url. They check the request sent, the success statuses (201 for REST, 200 for `exportIdentifiers.form`), and that error statuses fail.
- Controller tests check that it only skips authenticating when already authenticated as the requested user (ignoring case, as login does).
- `mvn package` passes: 162 tests, 0 failures.
- Tested end to end on OpenMRS Platform 2.8.10 with authentication 2.5.0-SNAPSHOT (2FA). One server with this change issued identifiers from its sequential generator, with `exportIdentifiers.form` excluded from CSRF protection. Two other servers refilled their pools from it at the same time:
  - one without this change, using `exportIdentifiers.form`
  - one with this change, using the REST url

  All identifiers came from the server's sequence, with none issued twice.

title: Upgrade to support OpenMRS Platform 3.0
body:
Updates idgen so it builds against, and runs on, openmrs-core master (Platform 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT: Java 21, Jakarta EE, Spring 7, Hibernate 7). Same approach as the platform 3 upgrades of calculation (openmrs/openmrs-module-calculation#19), legacyui and webservices.rest. The module version moves to 7.0.0-SNAPSHOT. Master's 6.0.0-SNAPSHOT is the unreleased Platform 2.8 line from #130 (with IDGEN-137), which PIH's pihcore builds against, so that line continues on the `6.x` branch, cut from 8f2918c.

## Changes
- Build and dependencies:
  - `openMRSVersion` is now 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT and `openmrs-bom` is imported.
  - Java 21 with `-parameters`.
  - The explicit `mockito-inline` / `byte-buddy` pins are removed; core's test stack provides Mockito 5.
  - `httpclient` is now `provided`. Core's war already ships 4.5.14, and the omod was bundling older httpclient/httpcore/commons-codec copies.
  - `openmrs-web` is now only on the omod. On the api test classpath it pulled core's MVC config into the api context, which then failed with "No ServletContext set".
  - The omod now uses webservices.rest 5.0.0-SNAPSHOT and legacyui-omod 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT. `javax.servlet-api` is dropped.
- `config.xml`: `require_version` is now 3.0.0.
- `HibernateIdentifierSourceDAO`:
  - All Hibernate Criteria queries are now JPA `CriteriaBuilder`. Unique lookups still use `uniqueResult()`, so a duplicate still throws.
  - Saves go through `HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate` and return the managed instance; deletes use `remove`.
  - Native SQL uses `createNativeQuery` / `createNativeMutationQuery`, and `IntegerType.INSTANCE` becomes `StandardBasicTypes.INTEGER`.
  - The `getQuantityInPool` HQL used column names (`pool_id`, `date_used`), which Hibernate 7 rejects. It now uses property paths.
  - `refreshIdentifierSource` only refreshes a source that is in the current session. Hibernate 7's `refresh()` rejects a detached instance, which Hibernate 5 reattached, so `generateIdentifiers()` threw for a source loaded in an earlier session after it had already generated and logged the identifier.
- `moduleApplicationContext.xml`: core 3.0 has no `patientServiceTarget` bean. idgen's three Luhn validators are now `putAll`-ed into core's `identifierValidators` map, the same map `PatientServiceImpl` autowires. `IdentifierValidatorRegistrationTest` checks that core rejects a wrong check digit for each of them, because core accepts any identifier when it can't find the validator.
- `IdentifierSource.hbm.xml`:
  - The `RemoteIdentifierSource.user` column is quoted, because `USER` is reserved in H2 2.x and the table was never created in tests.
  - `native` generators become `identity`, matching core 3.0's own mappings. Hibernate 7's `native` uses a sequence on PostgreSQL, but idgen's tables use auto-increment.
- `IdgenTask`: `Daemon.runInDaemonThread(Runnable, token)` was removed from core. It now calls `Daemon.runInDaemonThreadWithoutResult`.
- Imports: commons-lang becomes lang3, and javax.servlet becomes jakarta.servlet.
- Tests: the remaining JUnit 4 tests are migrated to Jupiter.
  - The `@Rule ExpectedException` checks in `IdentifierSourceRestControllerTest` and `LogEntrySearchHandlerTest` become `assertThrows`, because Jupiter has no rules.
  - The `shouldGetAll()` overrides in `IdentifierSourceRestControllerTest` and `LogEntryControllerTest` are removed. They had no `@Test`, which Jupiter needs on an override, so they had stopped running; without them the inherited test runs in both classes.
  - `RemoteIdentifierSourceProcessorTest` stays skipped (it was `@Ignore`, now `@Disabled` with the same reason).
- CI: Bamboo job and docker image, plus `release.yml`, now use JDK 21.

## Verification
- `mvn clean install` passes against the published core 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT: api 54 tests (3 skipped, all already skipped on master), omod 99 tests. Apart from the two new tests, every test class runs the same number of tests as on master.
- On Tomcat 11 with MySQL 8 and core 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT, idgen 7.0.0-SN

title: IDGEN-137: IDGen should refill pool if not enough identifiers available
(docs) Replace the dead Travis badge with the GitHub Actions one
body:
The README badge still points at travis-ci.org, which shut down and now redirects to a 404, so the badge renders blank. This module builds on GitHub Actions via build.yml, so this points the badge and its link there.

Heads up that the badge will show red right now: the latest build.yml run on master failed on 2026-09-03 on the OWASP dependency check job, not the Maven build.
